picks.excerpt: UBTech launched its first full-size Ultra-Bionic humanoid robot at a Shenzhen event, pushing an AI-driven consumer humanoid — with the company floating the unsettling ambition of making robot replicas of loved ones.
picks.rationale: A full-size consumer humanoid marks a concrete step in physical AI hardware and the embodiment questions designers of robot UX will grapple with next; novel launch from a credible outlet, distinct from every other pick's topic.

picks.excerpt: Solos unveiled the camera-free AirGo A6 AI glasses plus an AirGo V2 Privacy Kit that physically covers the 16MP camera lens, keeping onboard AI voice assistant and live translation while addressing bystander privacy fears around always-on smart glasses.
picks.rationale: A physical privacy-mode kit reframes how wearable-AI designers can resolve the always-on capture vs. bystander-trust tension; fresh product news and a distinct take from the Meta privacy-LED cluster already published.

picks.excerpt: Sony revived its bridge camera line with the RX10 V, whose onboard BIONZ XR AI processor drives real-time recognition autofocus that automatically identifies birds and animals, alongside 4K/120fps capture and 30fps burst shooting.
picks.rationale: On-device AI recognition autofocus is directly actionable for creators shooting reference and product imagery; novel hardware release, distinct camera topic from the other picks.

picks.excerpt: Amazon brought AI reading tools to Kindle first via the iOS app — 'Ask this Book,' a spoiler-free chatbot that answers plot and character questions, and 'Story So Far,' which generates summaries tailored to your current reading position.
picks.rationale: Amazon shipping generative AI reading features (spoiler-free chatbot, position-aware summaries) is a concrete pattern designers of content apps can learn from; app-first rollout is fresh and a fourth distinct topic and outlet.
